guarantees.claim: Each bit of async_fault_d is continuously driven by its corresponding direct error input: e.g., async_fault_d[AsyncFaultKmacCmd] = kmac_cmd_err_i, etc.
async_fault_d[AsyncFaultFsmIntg] is the OR of ctrl_fsm_err_i, data_fsm_err_i, and op_fsm_err_i.
async_fault_d[AsyncFaultFsmChk] is the OR of state_change_err_i and op_state_cmd_err_i.
async_fault_o is the bitwise OR of async_fault_q and async_fault_d.
error_o[ErrInvalidOp] is gated by op_done_i: it equals sync_err_o[SyncErrInvalidOp] when op_done_i is high, else 0.
error_o[ErrInvalidIn] is gated by op_done_i: it equals sync_err_o[SyncErrInvalidIn] when op_done_i is high, else 0.
error_o[ErrShadowUpdate] is directly driven by async_err_o[AsyncErrShadowUpdate] without op_done_i gating.
fault_o[FaultKmacOp], FaultKmacOut, and FaultSideSel are gated by op_done_i: each equals its corresponding sync_fault_o bit only when op_done_i is high, else 0.
fault_o bits FaultKmacCmd through FaultKeyEcc are driven directly from the corresponding async_fault_o bits without op_done_i gating.

assumptions.claim: op_done_i is asserted only when a valid operation has completed and is deasserted when no operation is active.
assumptions.risk: If op_done_i is asserted spuriously, invalid sync_err_o or sync_fault_o bits can be forwarded to error_o/fault_o, triggering false alarms or security responses.

assumptions.claim: sync_err_o[SyncErrInvalidOp] and sync_err_o[SyncErrInvalidIn] are stable and valid at the time op_done_i is high.
assumptions.risk: If these signals change before op_done_i, the error may be missed; if they change after, glitches or stale values may cause misreporting. Missing a genuine error could allow a fault to go undetected.

assumptions.claim: async_fault_q is cleared by external logic when faults are acknowledged or cleared.
assumptions.risk: If async_fault_q is never cleared, async_fault_o will remain high permanently after a fault, potentially locking the system in an unrecoverable error state.

assumptions.claim: The constant indices (e.g., AsyncFaultKmacCmd) align with the bit positions of async_fault_d/async_fault_o vectors; no out-of-bounds access occurs.
assumptions.risk: If a configuration mismatch occurs, wrong signals may be assigned, leading to incorrect fault reporting and potentially bypassing security checks.

uncertain_points.claim: The clearing mechanism for async_fault_q is not visible in this chunk; if clearing is incomplete or late, async_fault_o can remain asserted indefinitely, preventing recovery from transient faults.
uncertain_points.risk: Permanent fault assertion may cause denial-of-service or force repeated security responses, impacting availability and safety.

uncertain_points.claim: Sync error bits (SyncErrInvalidOp, SyncErrInvalidIn) are only forwarded when op_done_i is high; if they are set and cleared before op_done_i rises, the error is silently lost.
uncertain_points.cond: error occurs and clears before operation done
uncertain_points.risk: Transient or intermittent faults may go unreported, allowing a security violation to pass undetected.

uncertain_points.claim: The security countermeasure 'CTRL.FSM.CONSISTENCY' maps only to a simple OR of state_change_err_i and op_state_cmd_err_i into one fault bit. It is unclear if separate reporting or latching is required.
uncertain_points.risk: Loss of error detail may hinder diagnosis of FSM integrity failures, possibly allowing a sophisticated attack to remain hidden.

uncertain_points.claim: ECC fault (FaultKeyEcc) is driven directly from async_fault_o without any qualification; a transient ECC error could permanently set the fault output if async_fault_q is not cleared.
uncertain_points.risk: Persistent fault flag may cause unnecessary key invalidation or shutdown actions.
